1.11.1: The skill leads with the rule that always applies: **write mrkdwn, every time**. 1.11.0 put a converter inside `post`, and the asterisks kept arriving - which is how it became clear the messages were never going through `post` at all. A converter cannot reach text a model writes straight into a reply. A skill can.
1.11.0: `post` writes mrkdwn itself. Only the shapes that are never valid mrkdwn are converted - `**bold**`, `# heading`, `[text](url)` - so a message that was already correct passes through untouched.
1.10.0: `post` was the last way bytes could be typed into a tool call: `attachments` took base64. The agents' surface takes a key now. Every tool here was audited for this, and this was the one that did not look like an argument.
1.9.0: A thread says what is attached to each message. A file somebody uploaded three messages ago was invisible to an agent reading the conversation - the text said "have a look at this" and there was nothing to look at.
1.8.0: `readAttachment` hands a model the key for bytes and the text for text, which is the one place that split is not symmetrical: text is the answer, bytes never are.
1.7.1: No code changed. `category` became `tags` in every manifest here, and a manifest field is a patch.
1.7.0: Says what it is for, so the marketplace filter has something to show.
1.6.0: The agents' `uploadBinary` has nowhere to put bytes; the function still does. A run had answered a png and a key and then written five thousand characters of base64 into the next call by hand.
1.5.1: The skill says to send the picture, not the markup. It had been telling a model to upload a diagram with a `.svg` filename - right when `mermaid_render` only answered markup, wrong once it answered a picture, and Slack draws no SVG.
1.5.0: Takes a key, falls back to the configured connection, and says which door is which. Four things, all of them found by a message that went wrong.
1.4.0: A drawing travels by key rather than through the model. A few kilobytes of base64 written back out by hand does not arrive intact.
1.3.0: `userToken` beside the bot token, because search needs a user token and uploads need the bot's. `post` can attach a file to upload rather than only a permalink to one already there.
1.1.0: Signature verification goes through the platform's crypto API; the hand-written hashing is gone.
1.0.0: First release. Posts, replies in threads, searches, reads a conversation, and uploads files.
